title: How a bridge hangs
summary: A suspension bridge doesn't stand on its deck. It hangs from two cables, and the cables pull on the ground at each end.

sections.title: Built in the order it carries

c.md: **Two towers.** They carry almost all of the bridge's weight, straight down into the riverbed.
**The main cable** is draped over both towers and tied into concrete anchorages on the banks.
**Hangers** drop from the cable at regular intervals, like the strings of a harp.
**The deck** is hung from the hangers. It never pushes on the towers; it pulls on the cable.
**Add a load.** The truck's weight runs up the hangers, along the cable, over the towers and down into the ground.

# Tension
A cable can only pull. That is why it can be so thin and still carry a road.
